newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Tesco sees sales rising further.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Tesco sees sales rising further.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc hopes to be able to push sales growth ahead further in the second half of the year from its current 7.5 percent like-for-like rise, chairman Sir Ian MacLaurin told Reuters.
"I would expect us to (be above 7.5 percent)," he said in a telephone interview.
MacLaurin said Tesco's initiatives on a wide range of factors including price and service and a stronger UK economy should help push sales forward.
"There will be more developments coming," he said.
But he said operating margins had fallen by around 0.3 percentage points in the first half.
"Inflation (in stores) is around three percent and going south (down) at the moment," he said.
Tesco launched an "Unbeatable Value" campaign on 600 selected items over its regular price offers earlier this month.
But MacLaurin said he did not think supermarkets were about to enter a price war. "No, I don't think we are...prices are important...but they are only part of the equation," he said.
MacLaurin said the company would continue to look for opportunities for expansion abroad but "at the end of the day we have to ask whether it benefits shareholders."
He said dividend increases were likely to continue at around current levels of 6.5 percent or so, closer to earnings per share growth as indicated earlier this year.
Tesco turned in half year pretax profits of 321 million stg, up from 290 million stg previously, on turnover of 6.75 billion stg and paid out a dividend of 3.25 pence, up from 3.05 pence.
